additional_info.subject: URGENT: SiCharge D Mainbreaker_QA1 faults causing repeated session drops and reboots – Sandy Road Galway
additional_info.body:
Hi Siemens Support:
We are requesting urgent assistance regarding a Siemens SiCharge D unit at our Sandy Road site in Galway, Ireland, which is experiencing repeated customer impacting faults.
Charger details
Model Siemens SiCharge D
ChargePoint ID 170003303
Location Sandy Road, H91X7PD, Galway, Ireland
Issue summary
Multiple customer sessions are starting and charging normally, then stopping automatically after approximately 10 to 20 minutes. Following these session drops, both connectors enter Unavailable state and the charger performs a coordinated reboot.
Diagnostics evidence
GreenFlux OCPP diagnostics and Siemens vendor payloads confirm the following sequence on 19 January 2026
• Both connectors simultaneously report VendorErrorCode Mainbreaker_QA1
• The charger initiates PerformingCollaboratedReboot across both EVSEs
• Post reboot, both connectors report secc is initializing
• Backend connectivity remains online throughout
• No remote stop, reset, or availability commands are issued by the platform
This confirms that sessions are being terminated by a cabinet level protection event inside the charger rather than by backend, app, or payment systems.
Impact
The charger is intermittently unusable and customer confidence at a flagship site is being materially affected. This site is live and high visibility, and the issue is now recurring.
Request
We require urgent Siemens support to
Confirm the technical meaning and trigger conditions of Mainbreaker_QA1 on SiCharge D
Advise whether this fault typically indicates an internal breaker or QA1 sensing module issue versus an external supply condition
Review charger internal logs and diagnostics remotely if possible
Confirm whether a Siemens site visit or component replacement is required tonight.
We can provide full OCPP payloads, timestamps, and screenshots immediately if required.
Given the customer impact and clear evidence of repeated cabinet level protection faults, we would appreciate this being treated as a priority case within our 4 hour qualified response time SLA and onsite site visit tonight.
regards,
Colin

additional_info.subject: ID0473217-DC/Si-D/IE-[MP / S2 170003303]  Main breaker Fault CRM:03277000065
additional_info.body:
Dear Service Coordinator / RC,
I am writing to inform that we are moving the case
0473217
﻿from the Technical Support to the eMobility RC-XX SI E Queue. We kindly ask you to take over the case and perform the necessary troubleshooting steps.
Customer:
Product:
Sicharge D - Charging Center
Main Asset:
MP/S2170003303
Charger ID / Serial No.:
7hSoEi
Charger address/functional location:
Priority:
Medium
Handover reason:
The client has reported an issue with the Main Breaker (QA1) not closing. Please attend site, carry out the following steps.
First is to check if the XD9.1 is inserted tightly. These are those loose connectors.
Second is by applying (or checking) 24V on the QA28 and then QA29, we should be able to get 230V until the input of both L+ and ON in the MA1, from the logic below:
If we apply 24V on the A1-A2 and the contact 11-14 doesn't close then we need to replace QA29, same process with QA28
Next thing is to check 24V on the Under-voltage relay, the QA1 feedback should not be closing so you must not have 24V between .1 and .4.
The 24V to the UVR are supplied by QA26:
Next question, when you reach the site, what is the LED colour of the ACT and TRIP in the QA1? (seen from the front)
If both LEDs are on, then that means MA1 is faulty and needs replacement.
If everything above checks out properly and it still doesn't work (230V in MA1, QA26 sending 24V, 24V in KF5 - first photo and KF2, for QA29 and QA28 - second photo). Please measure on the output of the QA1 if any phase is not having the 230/380V:
If we don't have a phase or multiple phases, then we need to replace the QA1 but MA1 should not be necessary or the UVR.
If QA26 is not sending the 24V for the UVR, then we need to check which of these lines is not getting 24V:
If all of them checks out fine and we still don't have 24V in the output (24) then we need to replace the QA26.
I don't think it's the feedback of the QA1 since we don't have the error called "Failure in Feedback line".
Usually when we have these kinds of problems it's the MA1 but let's prove it.
My recommendation is to take a spare MA1, QA26, QA28/29 (they are the same) and UVR. Let me know if you think you should take a QA1, I can recommend it too.
Following our previous analysis, we identified that the issue is related to the FC16. At the moment, there are no active errors on the charger, and everything is functioning normally.
If the error is currently live on your side, we can arrange for a technician to visit the site and perform a check.
For now, we will keep the charger under monitoring. If the error appears again, we can proceed with a site visit and replace the FC16 if necessary.
Kindly pick up the case using "Pick" option in the queue or manually using the "Assign" function from the
eMobility RC-XX SI E Queue
and work on it & document the activity (Logs/Field Service Report) and attach it to the case under Documents Tab on ISP.

additional_info.subject: Re: ID0473217-DC/Si-D/IE-[MP / S2 170003303]  Main breaker Fault CRM:02888000551
additional_info.body:
Dear Ivan,
Thank you for the update.
For clarity, advising that the issue has been forwarded to the local support team to be handled in the coming days does not provide a qualified response for a priority incident at a live public charging site.
As outlined in our earlier emails, this unit has experienced repeated Mainbreaker_QA1 faults with coordinated reboots, resulting in multiple mid-session customer failures. In the absence of any technical assessment or interim operational guidance from Siemens, we have taken the decision to set connectors 170003303-1 and 170003303-2 offline to prevent further customer impact.
At this stage, we need the following from Siemens engineering rather than case forwarding:
• An initial technical assessment of the Mainbreaker_QA1 fault
• Guidance on whether the charger should remain offline pending investigation
• Confirmation of next steps, including whether on-site intervention or component replacement is anticipated
Please confirm when a qualified engineer will review the logs and revert with actionable guidance.
Regards,
Colin
Colin Barry
Brite EV charging
